record.text: How do EU-funded projects that set out to measure a property of the antihydrogen atom itself differ in which property each aims to measure and by what apparatus?
record.reference_answer: Two projects set out to measure a property of antihydrogen itself, and they target different properties with different apparatus. ANGRAM aimed at a 30% measurement of the gravitational acceleration for antihydrogen - enough to reveal the sign of gravity acting on antimatter and test the Weak Equivalence Principle - by rotating a three-grating moire deflectometer coupled to a detector, a scheme that requires neither position resolution nor time-of-flight information; the atoms were to be made in the AEgIS apparatus by three-body recombination of antiprotons and positrons, but only a signal consistent with production of antihydrogen atoms was reported, after the end of the beam time, so the gravity measurement could not be carried out, and the project further found that Rydberg-state antihydrogen interacts too heavily with the atoms of material gratings for material gratings to be usable. QUARTET measures a spectroscopic property instead: the classical Lamb shift, a transition in the microwave region, with antihydrogen spectroscopy planned on the ELENA beamline at CERN alongside a parallel muonium campaign at PSI; if no difference from matter is observed the measurement gives the first determination of the antiproton charge radius. Their apparatus differs accordingly - a rotating grating interferometer and annihilation detector for the free-fall measurement in ANGRAM, a microwave spectroscopy setup commissioned with protons and then adapted to the GBAR beamline for QUARTET.

record.text: How do metabolites produced by the gut microbiota after bariatric surgery affect the host, according to EU-funded research?
record.reference_answer: Two projects trace a metabolite of the post-surgery gut microbiota to an effect on the host. EnteroBariatric reports that Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) shifts the microbiome from Firmicutes to the Proteobacteria phylum and raises faecal Enterobacteriaceae, and that metabolites of the RYGB-associated microbiota - notably tyramine, which can come directly from diet or be produced by intestinal Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcaceae - promote colon cancer risk via increased DNA damage, cell proliferation and inflammation. Drug the bug runs the other way: the surgery-altered microbiota produces less imidazole propionate, a histidine-derived metabolite made by the microbial enzyme UrdA (urocanate reductase) that is elevated in prediabetes and type 2 diabetes and induces insulin resistance, so the project synthesized and screened more than 40 compounds seeking inhibitors of that enzyme as a new class of diabetes medication. In both, a molecule produced by the post-surgery gut microbiota is the proposed mediator of a host outcome: in Drug the bug the altered microbiota may be directly linked to some of the metabolic improvements observed following surgery, with imidazole propionate reduced after surgery, while in EnteroBariatric metabolites produced by RYGB-associated gut microbiota modulate the colorectal cancer risk.

record.text: Some proteins have no fixed folded structure, yet proteins of this kind are what carry certain tiny animals and their cells through the loss of virtually all their water. How are EU-funded projects working out which features of such a protein's amino-acid sequence provide that protection?
record.reference_answer: Both projects treat protection against drying as something encoded in the sequence of proteins that never adopt a fixed structure, and both planned the same combination - large libraries of sequence variants, a score per variant, and machine learning to extract the rules - but each report records how far that plan actually got. The Desiccation Survival project starts from Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins of tardigrades, which under drying undergo glass-transition and gelation into vitrified solids that stop the cell's other proteins unfolding and aggregating, and planned computational analysis of known CAHS sequences, a designed library screened by a high-throughput survival assay, and machine-learning extraction of the features behind protective glass-transition; what its report describes as executed is an integrative analytical pipeline combining computational sequence analysis, structural characterization using NMR, solution biophysics and ensemble generation, membrane biophysics, yeast genetics and cell biology, through which it identified new protein sequences and features contributing to desiccation survival and uncovered the mechanism by which these IDPs achieve stress tolerance - the survival screen and the machine-learning step are not mentioned there. FLINDIP planned deep mutational scanning of tardigrade proteins essential for surviving complete desiccation, with cell libraries of hundreds of thousands of variants scored by competition assay; its report states that random-mutant libraries for the original target genes were built but the phenotype of Boothby et al 2017 could never be reproduced, so after the Covid-19 closure the work switched to desiccation-resistance proteins of the Late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) family from Liu et al., 2019, whose repeat-rich sequences complicated synthesis and whose new libraries were near finishing preparation at grant end, and that the planned experimental work on intrinsically disordered proteins could not be completed by the end of the grant. FLINDIP's analysis half did deliver: the reusable pipeline was built and demonstrated on a Kondrashov lab dataset of mutants versus phenotype for four green fluorescent proteins (GFPs), published as Sommermeyer et al., 2022, whose finding was that mutationally robust proteins are not optimal templates for machine-learning-driven protein design and that predictions are more accurate for mutationally fragile proteins.

record.text: Cheap ceramic magnets made from iron oxide are much weaker than the high-performance magnets that rely on hard-to-source imported metals. How do the EU-funded projects working to make the iron-oxide kind strong enough to take their place differ in their approaches?
record.reference_answer: Two projects take this on from opposite ends. AMPHIBIAN works at the materials level: it builds hybrid magnets that couple hard ferrite to a soft magnetic phase through magnetostatic interactions (patent P201600092), targeting up-scalable, cost-efficient fabrication of dense anisotropic ferrite-based magnets with 40% enhanced magnetic performance (energy products above 55 kJ/m3) over commercial ferrites; it reports a 40% increase in energy product, 50 kg of SrFe12O19-Fe hybrid magnets fabricated by Max Baermann, and a completely rare-earth-free flywheel as its substitution demonstrator. PASSENGER works at the industrial end, scaling improved strontium ferrite (Sr-ferrite) up a pilot line: 4 tones of improved Sr-ferrite were industrially produced in the first 18 months, and its report states that improving ferrite 'with no use of any critical raw material' overcame one of the main limitations of ferrite magnets, 'the risk that magnets might become demagnetized when operating in cold environments (below 0 C)', which matters for e-mobility in cold conditions. Its 8 innovative pilot plants at TRL 7 aim at up-scaled production (several tonnes per year) of REE-free permanent magnets with a major cost advantage by comparison NdFeB magnets, demonstrated in electromobility applications and water motor pumps, with the consortium given in its final report as 21 partners (14 companies) from 8 countries; the same programme also runs a manganese-aluminium-carbon (MnAlC) line, which is context for the project rather than part of the iron-oxide answer. The contrast is therefore one composite-magnet concept carried from proof-of-concept to a single energy-storage demonstrator, against an industrial scale-up of ferrite itself to pilot-plant volumes and vehicle-grade robustness.

record.text: How have EU-funded businesses tried to earn money by bringing older people who feel lonely together with other people in person?
record.reference_answer: Two EU-funded ventures sell company itself rather than a device. The Freebird Club (FreeBC_Orgs) runs a membership-based peer-to-peer social travel and homestay club exclusively for older adults: members travel and stay with each other for a nightly rate inside a trusted community of senior peers, so a host earns income while both sides get companionship, and the project extended the club from individual to organisational membership so age-sector bodies could bring in the 'harder to reach' seniors - piloted by bringing a group of 12 older adults from the London Irish Centre's Senior Wellbeing Service to stay with local hosts in Kerry, Ireland. ADOPT GRANDPARENTS works in the opposite direction, pairing elderly people living in care homes with youngsters for supervised shared visits and activities under a Social & Education Training Programme; after three years as a non-profit, Intergenerational Technologies SL was constituted as a company to run it as a social economy business, launched in Spain and Portugal and projecting growth to 242 employees and EUR 23,017,094 revenues by 2024. Both frame loneliness in later life as the market: Freebird also targets financial insecurity and the lack of travel options for seniors, while ADOPT GRANDPARENTS also aims at the loss of intergenerational contact for the young.

record.text: How do the projects whose central objective is to develop a cosmic-ray muon scanner for screening closed cargo containers and vehicles differ in what their scanners are built to detect?
record.reference_answer: Two projects have the muon scanner itself as their central objective, and they aim it at different threats. IMPRINT is built around the innovative Muon Detection System that Lingacom is developing, using high-energy natural atmospheric cosmic ray muon particles to look for high-Z materials used in nuclear bombs and shielded radioactive materials (used in 'dirty bombs') in containerized cargo and vehicles - the case where Radiation Monitors and X-ray fail on dense or high attenuating vehicles - and it reconstructs 3D imaging from muon data, with the aim of stopping insiders stealing material from nuclear and radioactive sites. SilentBorder develops and validates a cosmic-ray tomography (CRT) scanner for border guard, customs and LEAs whose target is much broader smuggling: hazardous and illegal goods (e.g. SNM), contraband such as tobacco or explosive, and hidden persons in up to 20' iso containers, exploiting the fact that cosmic-ray muons are highly penetrating, about 10,000 times the energy of a typical X-ray, to distinguish materials and give a visualised 3D image. So IMPRINT is a nuclear-security instrument narrowed to shielded high-Z material, while SilentBorder is a customs instrument that also has to find organic contraband and people.

record.text: Which projects use the wave-like motion of atoms as the measuring element in high-precision sensors of gravity and acceleration?
record.reference_answer: Six projects use atom (matter-wave) interferometry as the measuring element for precision gravity and acceleration measurement, spanning instrument building, sensitivity theory and commercial translation. MWGRAV pursued matter-wave gravitation sensors at SYRTE, noting that atom interferometers already compete with or beat inertial sensors built on other technologies, and targeting gravimetry, gradiometry, metrology and gravitational-wave detection. Dommigs designed a monolithic reflective interferometer with diffraction slabs cut into a silicon monolith, evaluated for prospecting gravimetry and for accelerometers for long-distance under-water navigation. TICTOCGRAV combined ultracold Cadmium and Strontium optical clocks with Bragg interferometers, aiming at tests of the weak equivalence principle below 10^-13, while MEGANTE probed the gravitational field with cold atoms in free fall to redetermine the gravitational constant G beyond torsion-balance and pendulum accuracy. On the enhancement and translation side, QBAS investigated theoretically how entanglement between atoms and photons could raise atom-interferometer sensitivity, pointing at gravity gradiometers for detecting mineral reserves, and SEQ funded an engineer at M Squared Lasers to develop a first-iteration magneto-optical trap into a stable atom interferometer and commercialise a gravimeter.

record.reference_answer: Eight projects set out to make bacteriophages themselves into an antibacterial product. For patients: PhagoPROD scales up the GMP manufacturing and GLP diagnostics behind Pherecydes Pharma's personalised phage therapy against antibiotic-resistant infections; PHARMS screens phages of resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, Helicobacter pylori and Haemophilus influenzae and engineers phage vectors into a battery of phage-based therapies; and CURE builds phage preparations as candidates for clinical testing in asthma, using phages to rebalance a dysbiotic airway microbiome. record.text: How do EU-funded research projects go about explaining what decides which role an individual ends up taking inside an insect colony?
record.reference_answer: Seven projects treat the assignment of roles inside an insect society as the thing to be explained, and they attack it at very different levels. Genomic and molecular work dominates: RoyalMess searches for the genes that fate a Messor ant embryo to become a queen or a worker under social hybridogenesis; MELCA uses the double-clonal longhorn crazy ant Paratrechina longicornis to separate the molecular signatures of sex from those of the queen-versus-worker caste; and CASTECON asks whether inter-caste genetic correlations stop queens and workers from each reaching their own optimal dimorphic phenotype, and whether queens manipulate worker phenotype in their own interests. Physiology and neurobiology supply a second angle: DRiveR tests whether dopamine carries the Queen Mandibular Pheromone (QMP) signal that inhibits ovary activity in honeybee workers, while resiliANT measured the lipid content of individual ants by Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and, with targeted starvation, established a causal relationship between fat content and division of labour. MechAnt takes a mechanical view, tying the cutting ability of differently-sized leaf-cutter workers to the ontogeny of task choice and testing whether leaf-cutter colonies are organised according to ergonomic criteria. Division is the broadest: it asks across species why labour is divided at all, and why species differ in the mechanism used to produce different phenotypes - genetic differences, environmental cues, or random assignment of roles.

record.text: Which projects build, pilot or test constructed wetlands - engineered planted treatment beds such as subsurface-flow wetlands, sludge treatment wetlands or microbial-electrochemical METlands - as part of their own water or wastewater treatment work, rather than only studying, modelling or restoring natural wetlands?
record.reference_answer: Fourteen projects put a planted wetland bed of their own to work on water. One group builds electro-enhanced wetlands: iMETland constructed and operated full-scale METland units - electroconductive biofilter beds worked by electroactive bacteria - for zero-energy urban wastewater treatment in small communities; ELECTRAMMOX reported constructed wetlands packed with electroconductive carrier material recovering nitrogen from source-separated urine, reaching NH4+ oxidation rates up to 284 mg N/L/d but only 43% N recovery; ELECTRA's solutions relied on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands, whose bed materials and electron-sink control improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw and secondary effluent. A second group uses the wetland as one stage of a larger train: AquaNES demonstrated constructed wetlands combined with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment as one of the natural-engineered combinations spread over its 13 demonstration sites in Europe, India and Israel, which also cover bank filtration and managed aquifer recharge; PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands +', a vertical subsurface flow CW combined with granular activated carbon and zeolite, from TRL 4 to TRL 6 in India; HYDROUSA coupled anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands and UV disinfection on three Greek islands; INCOVER's sludge treatment wetland yielded a soil conditioner meeting Spanish heavy-metal rules. The rest run wetlands as the core technology or as one tested option: ZIRONITRO is a constructed wetland removing 98% of nitrates from contaminated groundwater to make drinking water; INNOV automates alchemia-nova's vertECO indoor constructed-wetland unit for greywater reuse; NICE designed and constructed 15 pilots at 10 urban sites, among them constructed wetlands and rain gardens for stormwater, greywater and wastewater; INDIA-H2O validated its phyto-treatment capacity in a small wetland construction and built a larger one for wastewater at PDEU; WATERAGRI identifies, develops and tests farm constructed wetlands among its on-farm water retention and nutrient-recovery measures; DIVAGRI co-develops an artificial wetland with smallholders as one of seven bio-based technologies installed at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites in Sub-Saharan Africa, a water-saving technology alongside its sub-surface clay-based irrigation system; and in M2EX constructed wetlands were employed to treat digestate effluent and evaluated for recovering metals from wastewater.

MEMBERSHIP RULE (the axis, not the string): a project is IN when it installs, pilots or tests a planted wetland bed OF ITS OWN as a working unit handling a water stream - sewage, greywater, stormwater, groundwater, source-separated urine, farm drainage or runoff, or irrigation water - whatever word the project uses for it (constructed, artificial, treatment, METland, hybrid subsurface wetland). The wetland need NOT treat a named wastewater stream, and the literal word 'constructed' is not load-bearing. A project is OUT when it only studies, models, monitors, restores or writes about wetlands, or when a wetland it did not build is merely the setting or the motivation. Applied to the two agricultural cases in the same breath: 858375 WATERAGRI is IN - objective O4 'identify, develop and test affordable ... farm solutions such as ... farm constructed wetlands', report 'exploring nature-based methods (farm-constructed wetlands, controlled drainage, bio-inspired filters)' - a planted bed it develops and tests for on-farm water retention and nutrient recovery, not for sewage; 101000348 DIVAGRI is IN on exactly that rule - report summary 'Biotechnologies co-developed with smallholders at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites across the continent include a desalination greenhouse, artificial wetland, biogas digester, biochar kiln, a subsurface irrigation system, mobile biorefinery and intercropping', workPerformed 'Water saving technologies such as artificial wetlands and a sub-surface clay-based irrigation system have already caught the attention of farmers in the co-design phase ... record.text: Which projects build a microfluidic chip device that carries a working model of the human blood-brain barrier or neurovascular unit, either as the whole chip or as one compartment of a larger organ-on-chip system?
record.reference_answer: Thirteen projects put a working blood-brain barrier (BBB) or neurovascular unit (NVU) model inside a microfluidic chip, almost all justified by the failure of animal and static in vitro models to predict human drug transport into the brain. Most build a dedicated BBB/NVU device: NVU-Chip recapitulates the human NVU in a single microfluidic device and is the first to incorporate cyclic mechanical strain in a BBB model; NOVACHIP builds a scalable vessel-like BBB-on-a-chip from bioprinted endothelialized capillaries; NeuroVU adds real-time chemical and trans-endothelial electrical resistance sensing to an NVU Organ-on-Chip; SONGBIRD integrates 3D scaffolds carrying blood-brain barrier cells into a microfluidic barrier-on-chip screening platform; SweetBrain, DIANA and BrainChip4MED use NVU and brain-on-a-chip models for disease-mechanism work and for screening drugs and nanocarriers that must cross the BBB. Others reach the same structure from vascular or microfabrication engineering: VESCEL engineers hiPSC blood vessels in microfluidic chips and applies them on-chip to blood-brain barrier function, 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP's 3D-printed microfluidic devices generate and maintain living functional 3D models of the blood-brain barrier, BBBhybrid two-photon-prints a 1:1-scale biohybrid barriers-on-a-chip model of the brain tumour microenvironment with its blood neurovasculature, and FEBRIS builds 3D microfluidic devices coated with endothelial cells mimicking brain vessel networks to study blood-brain-barrier disruption in cerebral malaria. A third group carries the barrier as one compartment of a bigger chip: MINERVA's microbiota-gut-brain organ-on-a-chip platform, whose brain compartment hosts a complete Blood-Brain-Barrier model, and GUTVIBRATIONS' stacked gut-brain-axis organ-on-chip with a blood-brain layer.

Scope chosen because the corpus-wide organ-on-chip family (~60 projects by title/objective) has no enumerable boundary, while the BBB/NVU has a small set of literal names.
